audit.whatIsWrong: Row 0 gave level 1 to Sett while whys[0] and early both say Tryndamere's auto damage and Fury generation beat you there; rows 5 and 6 read Skill while whys[5], whys[6], spikes[3] and late all say he takes over once crit lands.
audit.why: Battle Fury converts every attack into crit chance, so the raw level-1 auto war is his; Sett owns 2 through 6; the crit item and an 80s rank-3 Undying Rage flip the side lane back.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Tryndamere, Sett, Sett, Sett, Sett, Tryndamere, Tryndamere across both layers, with phases[0].why, phases[5].why and phases[6].why rewritten so the reasons match their new sides.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns on either ultimate or on Bloodlust, and the first-item and two-item spikes were written as neutral.
audit.why: Undying Rage is 120/100/80s — the same numbers as The Show Stopper — so by rank 3 he has an answer up as often as you have an engage. Bloodlust is a flat 12s.
audit.corrected: Numbers added to breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, phases[5].why, phases[6].why, spikes[0].text and mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: Mocking Shout was never mentioned anywhere on the page, and the spin was called his Q in two places.
audit.why: Mocking Shout (14s, 850 range) cuts your AD and slows ONLY enemies with their backs turned to him — so the retreat itself is what gets you killed; back off facing him. And the spin is Spinning Slash (E, 12s at rank 1); Bloodlust is the Q heal. Getting the slots wrong points the trade advice at the wrong cooldown.
audit.corrected: Written into report[5].t and breakdown.cooldowns; slots fixed in spikes[0].text, spikes[1].text, wants.you[1] and mid.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tryndamere.json (W text cd 14 range 850; E Spinning Slash cd 12/11/10/9/8; Q Bloodlust)

audit.whatIsWrong: mid claimed he is 'very gankable with no dash' while spikes[1] simultaneously warned he could 'spin to a wave'.
audit.why: Both cannot be true. Spinning Slash is his escape on a 12s rank-1 cooldown — the gank window is when it is spent, not permanent.
audit.corrected: mid rewritten to key the gank window to Spinning Slash's cooldown.

audit.why: Executioner's Calling is already the first back, which is the answer to Bloodlust.

edits.before: - Tryndamere Undying Rage: matchup-defining — Unkillable 5s. Wait it out, then all-in. Track it before every engage.
edits.after: - Tryndamere Undying Rage: 120s at rank 1 — wait the 5s out. - Tryndamere Mocking Shout: 14s; it slows only if your back is turned.

edits.before: Unkillable 5s. Wait it out, then all-in. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: 120s at rank 1. Wait the 5s out, then E-stun him before Bloodlust heals.

edits.before: Track Tryndamere's Undying Rage: Unkillable 5s. Wait it out, then all-in. When it is down — E-stun + W him.
edits.after: Mocking Shout slows only if your back is turned — retreat facing him, then E-stun into the W panel when R is spent.

edits.before: Double-punch passive makes you the strongest level-1 auto-trader in the lane. Punish Tryndamere on every CS, but respect his opening tool — chips now, all-ins later.
edits.after: Battle Fury turns every attack into crit chance, so his level-1 auto trade beats yours. Farm the level, bank Grit off his chip, and wait for Knuckle Down at 2.

edits.before: Stridebreaker fixes your only weakness — sticking to Tryndamere. Shove, recall on the spike, and force the next trade before he matches your item.
edits.after: His crit item out-paces your Stridebreaker: Bloodlust heals off a flat 12s and Fury keeps feeding it. Shove, recall, and take short trades only.

edits.before: Sterak's makes your all-in nearly unburstable. Fights are decided by whether you cash a max-grit W — track Undying Rage and commit on the gap.
edits.after: Sterak's keeps you alive, but Undying Rage on 80s at rank 3 negates your kill threat entirely. Play the teamfight, not the side-lane duel.

edits.before: With E rank you can pull Trynda in mid-Q spin: land Facebreaker at max range, follow with W once your Grit bar is full, and he can't out-sustain a full combo before his Q heal is up.
edits.after: With E rank you can pull him out of Spinning Slash: land Facebreaker at its 490 range, cash W on a full Grit bar, and Bloodlust's flat 12s cooldown cannot out-heal the combo.

edits.before: Your R The Show Stopper slams him but does nothing about Undying Rage — bait his ult, then suppress and displace him after the 5s invuln so he can't spin to a wave.
edits.after: The Show Stopper does nothing about Undying Rage — bait the 5s out first, then slam him away from his wave while Spinning Slash, 12s at rank 1, is still down.

edits.before: Levels 2-5 are your window: E-W-Q combos plus Grit sustain out-trade his spins before his Q heal recovers, and he's very gankable with no dash. Land Facebreaker to pull him and cash the CC.
edits.after: Levels 2-5 are your window: E-W-Q combos plus Grit sustain out-trade him before Bloodlust's 12s heal recovers, and he is gankable whenever Spinning Slash is down. Land Facebreaker and cash the CC.

edits.before: E slow to stick him through his Q spin
edits.after: E slow to stick through Spinning Slash
